native_mcp_support.notes: MCP is supported via Qwen-Agent framework. Model cards show explicit MCP configuration examples using mcpServers config in Qwen-Agent's function_list. Not a native model-protocol feature but rather framework-level support.

skills_concept.notes: Qwen-Agent is the agentic framework for Qwen models. It supports a function_list for tools/plugins, MCP server configs, and built-in tools (web search, code interpreter). Skills are loaded per-agent invocation (always_on per agent session), injected into system prompt and tool definitions.

release_date.notes: Citation in model card states month=April, year=2026; HF collection updated Apr 22

knowledge_cutoff.notes: Qwen team has not published an exact knowledge cutoff for Qwen3.6. Community discussions for the Qwen3 series suggest late-2023/early-2024 for some data subsets; Qwen3.5 technical report (Feb 2026) does not state a cutoff date explicitly. Value left null.

context_window_tokens.notes: Model card states: 'Context Length: 262,144 natively'. Default serving context length. Shared input+output pool.

input_output_shared.notes: Standard transformer architecture; context window is a shared pool for input + output tokens combined.

max_input_tokens.notes: Derived: context_window (262144) minus recommended max_output (81920). No hard vendor-published max_input cap; in practice the operator sets it via the serving framework.

max_output_tokens_default.notes: Model card Best Practices recommends max_tokens=32768 for most queries.

max_output_tokens_max.notes: Model card examples use max_tokens=81920 for complex problems; serving is set by operator via --max-model-len.

extended_context.notes: Model card states '262,144 natively and extensible up to 1,010,000 tokens' using YaRN RoPE scaling. Requires modifying rope_parameters in config.json or passing CLI overrides to vLLM/SGLang. Static YaRN may degrade short-text performance.

reasoning_tokens_count_as_output.notes: Qwen3.6 generates <think>...</think> reasoning blocks before the final response. These count toward output token budget and are billed as output tokens on DashScope.

tokenizer_family.notes: Qwen models use tiktoken-based BPE tokenization. The Qwen3 series shares the same tokenizer; vocabulary is 151,643 regular tokens + special/control tokens. Token embedding dimension uses padded 248320.

tokenizer_access.notes: Can be loaded via HuggingFace transformers AutoTokenizer. Underlying tokenizer uses tiktoken library with a custom vocabulary file. tokenizer.json available in HF repo.

count_tokens_method.value: from transformers import AutoTokenizer; tok = AutoTokenizer.from_pretrained('Qwen/Qwen3.6-27B'); len(tok.encode(text))

image_token_rule.value: Variable tile-based patching; number of tokens depends on image resolution and model's visual encoder tiling
image_token_rule.notes: Qwen3.6 uses a vision encoder with tile-based patching. Exact per-pixel token count formula not published in model card; differs from Qwen-VL's documented tile formula. Use AutoProcessor to count multimodal tokens.

audio_token_rule.notes: Qwen3.6-27B does not natively support audio input (text+image+video). Audio is handled by separate Qwen3-Omni / Qwen3.5-Omni models.

chars_per_token_estimate.notes: Rough estimate for English text using tiktoken BPE. Chinese text yields higher token density (~1.5 chars/token). Use AutoTokenizer for accuracy.

function_calling.notes: Qwen3.6 has strong function calling. vLLM/SGLang require --enable-auto-tool-choice --tool-call-parser qwen3_coder flag for structured tool output parsing.

native_mcp.notes: Qwen-Agent (the official agentic framework) accepts MCP server configs via mcpServers key in the function_list. MCP tool definitions are translated to Qwen function-call format and injected as input tokens.

parallel_tool_calls.notes: Qwen3 series supports parallel/multi-tool calls in a single turn via the OpenAI-compatible chat completions API. Confirmed by Qwen-Agent framework behavior.

max_tools_hard.notes: No hard API-enforced tool count cap documented for Qwen models. When self-hosted, the serving framework does not enforce a tool limit. Context window is the effective limit.

max_tools_practical.notes: No vendor-published empirical degradation point. Community consensus for capable models is ~30-50 tools before accuracy degrades; 40 is a conservative estimate. Qwen3.6's strong tool-use benchmarks (BFCL, MCPMark) suggest it may tolerate more than weaker models.

tool_definition_shape.notes: DashScope and self-hosted endpoints both use OpenAI-compatible chat completions API format. Tool definitions follow the OpenAI function-calling JSON schema. Qwen-Agent also supports a native Qwen tool format internally, but the OpenAI-compatible API path is standard for integrations.

tool_defs_count_as_input.notes: Tool definitions are serialized into the request and billed as input tokens. DashScope pricing page confirms: charged for input tokens and output tokens per request.

tool_search_deferral.notes: No documented tool-search or deferred-loading mechanism in vLLM/SGLang/Qwen-Agent equivalent to Claude's ENABLE_TOOL_SEARCH. Tools are injected in full at request time.

max_tool_name_len.notes: No documented character limit on tool names for Qwen models. Follows OpenAI function-call schema conventions.

tools_mcp.tool_schema_limits_notes: No documented schema-depth or per-tool-definition size limits. Practical limit is total input token budget. Qwen3.6 MCPMark benchmark score of 37.0 indicates reasonable performance with standard tool schemas.

max_tool_description_len.notes: No vendor cap; description counts against context window.

max_request_size.notes: No vendor byte cap; bounded by serving config (vLLM --max-model-len / --max-num-batched-tokens) and GPU memory.

max_tool_result_size.notes: Context-bound; tool results count against max_model_len.

max_parallel_tool_calls_count.notes: Depends on the model chat-template tool-call parser; see parallel_tool_calls.

tool_use_per_turn_limit.notes: Set by the agent host/framework, not the model.

max_total_tools.notes: No vendor cap. Effective ceiling ≈ (context_window − output headroom) ÷ avg tool-definition tokens, set by serving config. Client hosts may cap lower (Cursor ~40, Claude Desktop ~100).

tools_mcp.other_limits_notes: Open-weight: the model API layer imposes NO tool count/size caps. Binding limits come from (1) the serving stack — vLLM/SGLang max_model_len, max_num_batched_tokens, GPU KV-cache; (2) the model chat-template tool-call parser (must match --tool-call-parser); (3) the agent host (Cursor ~40-tool cap, Claude Desktop ~100). vLLM's default context is often 16K which silently truncates tool calls — raise --max-model-len.

strict_function_schema.notes: No OpenAI-style strict function-schema mode that enforces 100-prop/5-depth/no-oneOf. (Gemini/Anthropic have their own, looser keyword rules — captured in tool_schema_limits_notes.)

skills_supported.notes: No formal 'skills' packaging system analogous to Claude Agent Skills. Qwen-Agent provides an agent framework with tools/plugins injected per session, but there is no skills marketplace or packaged skill format.

skills_context.skills_context_cost_notes: No formal skills system. Tool definitions in Qwen-Agent are injected as input tokens at session start. MCP server tools are translated to OpenAI function format and count toward input budget.
skills_context.system_prompt_overhead_notes: System prompt is billed as input tokens. No fixed platform-injected system prompt overhead for self-hosted deployments. DashScope hosted API may inject a minimal system prompt; not documented.

prompt_caching.notes: DashScope hosted API supports Context Caching (prefix caching) for eligible models. qwen3-max and qwen3.5-plus support context cache discount on input tokens. For self-hosted vLLM/SGLang, prefix KV caching is available natively and reduces recomputation.

memory_feature.notes: No built-in persistent memory feature in Qwen3.6 model or DashScope API. Memory can be implemented externally via Qwen-Agent's memory modules, but these are not part of the model's context.

input_per_mtok_usd.notes: Qwen3.6-27B price not yet published on official Alibaba Cloud pricing page as of 2026-06-21. Third-party aggregator (pricepertoken.com, updated 2026-06-20) shows $0.14/M input for Qwen3.6-35B-A3B via Qwen API; the 27B dense model would likely be priced similarly or lower. Use as estimate only. Set to null for pure self-host compute.

output_per_mtok_usd.notes: Same source and caveat as input price. Approximate for Qwen API hosted endpoint. Self-hosted: cost = compute only.

cached_input_per_mtok_usd.notes: Cached input price per aggregator for Qwen3.6-35B-A3B. Official DashScope context-cache pricing for qwen3.5-plus in International mode shows ~60% reduction on input tokens for cached prefix.

batch_discount.value: 50% off input and output for Batch Invocation (async)
batch_discount.notes: Alibaba Cloud Model Studio pricing page explicitly states: 'If a model supports Batch Invocation, both input and output tokens are charged at 50% of the real-time inference price.' Applies to qwen3-max and qwen3.5-plus; Qwen3.6 batch support not confirmed on pricing page.

cost.multimodal_billing_notes: Image and video tokens on DashScope are billed as input tokens based on the visual encoder's patch/tile output. Exact per-image token count depends on resolution; use AutoProcessor to calculate. DashScope billing for Qwen3.5-Omni models documents separate audio rates; Qwen3.6-27B image/video rates are not separately published.

reasoning_billed_as_output.notes: DashScope pricing for qwen3-max shows 'CoT + response' for output pricing, indicating reasoning tokens are billed at the same output rate as the final response. The <think>...</think> block tokens count toward output billing.

license.notes: HF model card shows 'License: apache-2.0'. Apache 2.0 permits commercial use and redistribution.

param_variants.value: 27B dense (single size in Qwen3.6 dense lineup as of 2026-06-21)
param_variants.notes: Qwen3.6 release includes Qwen3.6-27B (dense, 27B params) and Qwen3.6-35B-A3B (MoE, 35B total / 3B active). This entry covers the 27B dense model.

native_context_config.notes: Model card states default context length 262,144 tokens. This is the max_position_embeddings in the model config.

max_context_documented.notes: YaRN RoPE scaling extends context to 1,010,000 tokens. Requires modifying rope_parameters in config.json (rope_type: yarn, factor: 4.0) or passing CLI overrides. Use --max-model-len 1010000 with VLLM_ALLOW_LONG_MAX_MODEL_LEN=1.

serving_frameworks.value: vLLM (>=0.19.0), SGLang (>=0.5.10), KTransformers, HuggingFace Transformers, Ollama (via quantized GGUF)

self_host.framework_tool_calling_notes: vLLM: add --enable-auto-tool-choice --tool-call-parser qwen3_coder for structured tool output. SGLang: add --tool-call-parser qwen3_coder. Both expose an OpenAI-compatible /v1/chat/completions endpoint. Qwen-Agent (pip: qwen-agent) provides higher-level MCP integration, translating MCP tool configs to Qwen function-call format. Thinking mode (default on) generates <think> blocks before tool calls; reasoning tokens count toward output budget.

models.notes: Qwen3.6-27B is the flagship dense model of the Qwen3.6 series, released April 2026 as a successor to Qwen3.5-27B. Notable for strong agentic coding (SWE-bench Verified 77.2, Terminal-Bench 59.3), multimodal support (text/image/video), and a Thinking Preservation mechanism that retains reasoning context across turns for reduced overhead in multi-turn agentic sessions.

models.notes: Qwen3.5-35B-A3B (released Feb 2026) is the predecessor to Qwen3.6-35B-A3B. The hosted DashScope equivalent is qwen3.5-flash ($0.10/$0.40 per M tokens, one of the most cost-effective hosted options). Strong agentic benchmarks: BFCL-V4 67.3, TAU2-Bench 81.2, BrowseComp 61.0. Differs from Qwen3.6 in not having Thinking Preservation and using /think /nothink soft switching.
